game: DEN@LAC Week 5 2026 (kickoff time, spread, total, venue roof and rest not in pack)

script.base: No saved spread or total, so the script is inferred from weeks 2-4 roles. Los Angeles should lean on Omarion Hampton (47 carries, 195 yards, 4.15 YPC over those three games) because Joe Alt, Trevor Penning and Kayode Awosika are out and Justin Herbert is poor versus pressure (EPA/dropback -0.32 when blitzed, -0.10 when not) against a Broncos defense that blitzes 39%. Denver allows 5.02 YPC and 15 runs of 10+, so Hampton's carries are the stable LAC path even if efficiency dips. Denver's ground game is J.K. Dobbins (38 carries, 125 yards, 3.29 YPC) into a better Chargers run defense (4.13 YPC, 11 runs of 10+), so Bo Nix may have to throw, but Nix is -0.30 EPA/dropback versus the blitz and the Chargers blitz 27%. Jaylen Waddle is the pass answer (23 targets, 183 yards, 264 air yards); R.J. Harvey is the checkdown (17 targets, 109 yards, -37 air yards), not a rusher (9 carries, 31 yards).
script.flip1: Pat Surtain II and Riley Moss are both out, so Herbert ignores the bad line and airs it to Tre Harris (15 targets, 189 yards, 206 air yards in three games; Quentin Johnston is out) in a shootout. Hampton's early-down volume dips only if Los Angeles is trailing and pass-first; Harris and Oronde Gadsden become the story and Denver's rush clock-kill never starts.
script.flip2: The Chargers' line collapse plus Denver's 39% blitz turns it into a sack slog. Hampton's YPC craters, Harris's 13.7 aDOT shots die, and the game stays low-event with Dobbins grinding short gains against a 4.13 YPC Chargers run defense.

injury_fallout: Official pre-game report, not the 90-minute inactives (not in pack). DEN CB Pat Surtain II out (ankle) and CB Riley Moss out (ribs): both starting corners gone, so LAC downfield options gain, chiefly Tre Harris, with Oronde Gadsden and Ladd McConkey (questionable, foot) next; Quentin Johnston is already out (chest; 13 targets, 91 yards, 198 air yards in weeks 2-4), so his share is the vacancy. LAC CB Donte Jackson out (hamstring) and S Derwin James out (hamstring): Denver deep/outside options gain, chiefly Jaylen Waddle (264 air yards) more than Courtland Sutton (212 air yards but only 75 yards). LAC OL Joe Alt out (neck), G Trevor Penning out (concussion), G Kayode Awosika out (fibula), G Branson Taylor questionable (neck): pressure up, rushing efficiency down, more quick throws — helps LAC RB/TE catches, hurts deep WR yards. Trey Lance doubtful (groin) is the backup; Herbert is the starter in the pack. Charlie Kolar, Scott Matlock and Rodney Shelley questionable; Brenen Thompson out. No Denver skill-position out in the report, so Dobbins keeps the carries and Harvey keeps the checkdowns. Sources: pack injury report plus weeks 2-4 target/carry splits.

The pass overlap (Waddle's 264 air yards into a Chargers defense missing a corner and Derwin James; Harris's 206 air yards into a Broncos defense missing Surtain and Moss) is real but fights the pressure script, and Waddle's line sits above a boom-bust median.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and Hampton under 41.5 lost the ticket: Alt, Penning and Awosika were out, Mitchell took the explosive carries (he already has a 52 and a 39), Denver's backup corners got cooked so Los Angeles threw, and Hampton finished on 10 carries at a crushed YPC — the 43-yard game showed the floor was already on the number, and the coin-flip price said the market had not missed this. Harvey over 26.5 lost the other leg because one 15-yard draw plus a short-yardage vulture, or a Dobbins snap limit that was not on the morning report, pushed a receiving back across a line the three-game sample made look free. Those counters are real, but they are not stronger than Dobbins owning 38 of the carries and Hampton still being the only back whose volume can survive a modest efficiency drop against a 5.02 YPC defense. If the OL counter feels stronger on Hampton alone, that leg is the one to pass, not Harvey.
slip_story: One story: lead-back volume, not a shootout stack. Los Angeles runs Hampton into the bad Denver run defense while Denver's rush work stays with Dobbins, so Harvey's rush line is a role mirage. Do not pair this with Waddle or Harris overs — those need the Surtain/Moss shootout flip and the opposite pressure script. No teaser, no TD, one market per player. This is a read, not a bet.
